source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Directions in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The post reports sparse-autoencoder feature replacement on the IOI task, but it does not test the GPT-2 small head circuit or any of the claim versions. It does not rely on that circuit finding.
record.gate_note: The post explicitly reports restoring uncorrupted IOI behavior by replacing features. Its tradeoff curve has no numerical values in the text. The findings concern SAE features, not the claimed attention-head classes or their roles.
record.test_reason: The post uses the IOI task (citing the original) as a testbed for sparse-autoencoder feature patching in Pythia models. It does not examine the 26-head circuit, backup heads, circuit reuse, method agreement on the circuit, or evaluation sensitivity of that circuit. It reports no head-level results, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that SAE features are more interpretable (by autointerpretability), more monosemantic, and better for precise steering and editing than comparable methods. The IOI feature-patching result is one illustration of this. They also note that SAEs leave nonzero reconstruction error.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse-autoencoder feature replacement rather than the original attention-head circuit analysis and criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says edit fine-grainedness increases with dictionary sparsity; it gives no numerical condition-specific IOI results in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching selected SAE dictionary features from clean into corrupted activations restores clean IOI behaviour. It is reported to be more precise than PCA, though the post gives no numbers. Because SAE reconstruction is imperfect, the patched model keeps a positive minimum KL divergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-autoencoder features allow sub-module, fine-grained causal edits that recover clean IOI behaviour in Pythia models.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The IOI result is summarized without numerical values, the model is not identified in the post's description of that result, and uncertainty is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical values are given for the IOI tradeoff curve, so none could be recorded as numbers. Other post results, including automatic-interpretability scores and feature examples, do not measure the IOI circuit claim.

untested.parts: All: the 26 heads, 7 classes and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not examined.
All: no name-mover ablation or backup-head analysis.
All: IOI is run on Pythia, but no head classes or roles are identified there.
All: SAE feature patching is not compared against the head circuit.
All: no evaluation of the circuit under different ablations, metrics or distributions.

record.verdict_notes: The model for the IOI experiment is not stated in the post. The linked paper (arXiv:2309.08600) would specify it. The automatic circuit discovery result concerns a parenthesis feature, not IOI.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small circuit, its 26 heads and 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
Whether backup heads take over after main name-mover heads are ablated.
Whether the same head classes and roles carry IOI in other models or are reused for other tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics recover the same circuit.
Whether the claimed circuit's faithfulness or completeness varies with ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
Whether the claimed circuit carries IOI across name orders, templates or more names.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Replace corrupted-datapoint activations with selected sparse-autoencoder feature activations from the clean datapoint.

conditions.value: selected dictionary features; exact selection and count not stated

rows.baseline: corrupted datapoint; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: The authors state that feature replacement can restore uncorrupted behavior; the tradeoff curve is not numerically described in the text.
rows.note: The post does not identify which model or models were used for this IOI result, so no model attribution is inferred.
rows.check: The row measures SAE feature patching restoring clean IOI behaviour, not any head circuit, so it bears on no version. The post's stated models are Pythia-70M/410M, but which one was used for IOI is not specified, so 'not stated' is acceptable. No numbers are given, so the state cannot be read against any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
